then.text: Our friend with the manifest! Every flight since has run on time, or near enough. I'd bet it was your clean handwriting.
Signed by the Loadmaster, and the distances from the Tower? Splendid. That's the Airbridge manifest done, and my phone has finally stopped ringing.
Have a few supplies from the stores, and the station's thanks. We don't hand out medals for paperwork, so you'll have to settle for tea.

else.text: The Tower gave you the distances? Lovely. Now the Loadmaster on the apron has to sign the manifest, and he only signs for people who can beat him in a fair fight. Don't ask me why.

then.text: Ask the Duty Controller in the Tower about the Airbridge distances, then have a word with the Loadmaster on the apron. Then come back.

else.text: Ah, a Champion with time on their hands. The Airbridge flies to the Falklands and back with a stop at Ascension, and every one of those flights is a mountain of paperwork.
Could you walk the manifest round for me? Tower first for the distances, then the Loadmaster on the apron for a signature. I'd do it myself, but I've got a phone that won't stop.

brz_loadsheet.text: Every aircraft has a weight and a balance. Passengers are weighed with their bags. Aid is weighed in tonnes. Post is weighed on a kitchen scale in the corner.
The Atlas can lift about thirty tonnes. The Voyager can carry nearly three hundred passengers or a lot of fuel. We try not to mix them.
